name: Sorghum

evidence.quote: Temperatures below freezing are detrimental to sorghum and may kill the plant.
evidence.doc: Sorghum Production, ARC-Grain Crops Institute (fact sheet, based on Sorghum Production Guide)

evidence.quote: Sorghum is normally planted with maize planters.
Normally sorghum is planted in South Africa from mid-October to mid-December.
temperate to warm weather (20 to 30 ºC) and a frost-free period of approximately 120 to 140 days

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Source gives this as the frost-free period the crop needs 'to exploit its inherit yield potential' (grain maturity), not a per-cultivar days-to-maturity table; early vs late hybrid maturity not broken out in this source (gap).

evidence.quote: sorghum is planted in 0.91 m, 1,5 m or 2.3 m rows
Table 2. Plant population and seed requirements for different row widths and in-row spacing / In-row spacing (mm) ... 10 ... 150
A planting depth of 25 mm is satisfactory with sufficient water. Under drier conditions the seed should be planted deeper, but no more than 50 mm.
Recommendations therefore, vary from 3.0 to 7.0 kilogram seed per hectare.

yield.conditions: national commercial average (mostly dryland, Free State & Mpumalanga), not a per-field target yield; smallholder/dryland yields likely lower

evidence.quote: The production of sorghum in South Africa varies from 100 000 tonnes (130 000 ha) to 180 000 tonnes (150 000 ha) per annum.

zoneNotes.karoo-arid: Source notes sorghum tolerates the drier, low-rainfall western production areas (~400 mm/yr) better than maize, but does not name Karoo-specific cultivars (gap).
zoneNotes.highveld: Free State and Mpumalanga (highveld/interior) are named as the largest sorghum production provinces.
zoneNotes.lowveld-bushveld: Source describes a general shift 'from the drier western production areas to the wetter eastern areas' and development of cold-tolerant cultivars, consistent with lowveld/bushveld conditions, but does not name specific zones or cultivars (gap).

gaps: No SA production-guideline PDF for sorghum was recoverable via Wayback (only an HTML redirect snapshot exists for the DAFF 'Brochure Sorghum.pdf'); ARC-GCI fact sheet and DALRRD Market Value Chain Profile 2020 used instead.
No per-cultivar days-to-maturity (early/medium/late) figures found; only the 120-140 day frost-free requirement.
No named cultivars/varieties by zone found in the sources reviewed (Grain SA/ARC-GCI cultivar list not located in this pass) — varieties field is empty.
Winter-rainfall (Western Cape), all-year (subtropical/coastal) and mild-frost sowing windows not addressed by the source; left empty rather than assumed.
Yield figure is a derived national average (total tonnes / total hectares), not a stated per-hectare recommendation from an agronomy source.
summary: ARC-GCI's Sorghum Production fact sheet (drawing on the DALRRD/DAFF Sorghum Production Guide) gives solid, quotable figures for SA planting window, row/in-row spacing, seed rate and sowing depth, and confirms frost kills the crop. Yield is only available as a derived national average, and no cultivar/variety list or per-cultivar maturity data was located, so verdict is partial rather than ready.
